Fact.Name: Form 8283 section choices
Fact.Description: The two sections printed on Form 8283: Section A and Section B.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B property types
Fact.Description: The printed Section B, Part I line 2 property-type choices.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B item letters
Fact.Description: The A, B, and C item identifiers printed in Section B, Part I and referenced by Parts II and III.

Fact.Name: Original reporting entity name, when different from the return name
Fact.Description: Form 8283 header, the name of the entity whose return originally reported this contribution, if different from the individual return name.

Fact.Name: Original reporting entity identifying number, when different
Fact.Description: Form 8283 header identifying number for the entity whose return originally reported the contribution, if different from the return shown above.

Fact.Name: Family pass-through entity contribution indicator
Fact.Description: Form 8283 header checkbox indicating that a family pass-through entity made the noncash charitable contribution.

Fact.Name: Noncash property contributions reported on Form 8283
Fact.Description: One contribution item or group of similar items per collection entry. A separate rendered copy per entry is an allowed way to use the form's one-or-more-copy instruction; entries retain the data needed for either Section A or Section B.

Fact.Name: Section used for this property item
Fact.Description: Whether this item is reported in Section A or Section B, based on the form's property and deduction rules. The module records the preparer's section choice. SINCE THE SECTION IS COMPUTED, this entry is read for ONE purpose only: a pass-through allocation, where the instructions require a member to complete the same section the entity completed, so the entity's section governs and no amount test applies. For every other item /form8283Items/*/sectionForPrinting decides the section from the printed rules and this entry is not read; an entry that disagrees with the computed section does not move it.

Fact.Name: Donee organization name
Fact.Description: Section A line 1 column (a), or the donee organization named for the Section B item.

Fact.Name: Donee organization address
Fact.Description: Address of the charitable organization receiving the contribution.

Fact.Name: Vehicle contribution checkbox
Fact.Description: Section A line 1 column (b), whether the donated property is a vehicle.

Fact.Name: Vehicle identification number
Fact.Description: Vehicle identification number for a donated vehicle unless Form 1098-C is attached.

Fact.Name: Description of donated property
Fact.Description: Property description for Section A column (c) or Section B, Part I, line 3 column (a); include the year, make, model, and mileage for a vehicle.

Fact.Name: Property condition at gift date
Fact.Description: Brief summary of the overall physical condition at the time of the gift, for tangible personal or real property in Section B.

Fact.Name: Date of contribution
Fact.Description: Section A column (d), date the property contribution was made. Typed as a calendar date, not free text, because the printed cell asks for one specific date (unlike ../writableDateAcquired, where "Various" is a printed valid entry). This is ordinarily a 2025 date; it is legitimately a prior-year date on a Form 8283 attached only because the return carries a charitable contribution carryover under IRC 170(d) (/writableForm8283RequiredForCarryoverYear true), where the instructions have the filer keep reporting the item from the year it was actually contributed.

Fact.Name: Date acquired by donor
Fact.Description: Date the donor acquired the property, as requested in Section A column (e) and Section B, Part I, line 3 column (d).

Fact.Name: How donor acquired property
Fact.Description: How the donor acquired the property, as requested in Section A column (f) and Section B, Part I, line 3 column (e).

Fact.Name: Donor's cost or adjusted basis
Fact.Description: Donor's cost or adjusted basis, requested in Section A column (g) and Section B, Part I, line 3 column (f). Section A says this column need not be completed for an item with a claimed deduction of $500 or less.

Fact.Name: Fair market value for Section A
Fact.Description: Fair market value reported in Section A column (h).

Fact.Name: Method used to determine fair market value
Fact.Description: Method used to determine fair market value, requested in Section A column (i).

Fact.Name: Section B property type
Fact.Description: Section B, Part I, line 2 category for the donated property.

Fact.Name: Certified historic structure NPS number
Fact.Description: National Park Service number when the Section B property is a certified historic structure.

Fact.Name: Appraised fair market value
Fact.Description: Section B, Part I, line 3 column (c), the appraised fair market value.

Fact.Name: Bargain sale amount received
Fact.Description: For a bargain sale, the amount received, Section B, Part I, line 3 column (g).

Fact.Name: Qualified conservation contribution relevant basis
Fact.Description: Relevant basis amount required for the qualified conservation contribution section B entry.

Fact.Name: Amount claimed as a deduction for this property item
Fact.Description: Amount claimed as a deduction, before income-limit carryover, in Section B, Part I, line 3 column (i). For Section A this carries the item's claimed deduction used in the filing-threshold total. A claimed deduction is never negative, and the Min 0 limit below says so at intake: this amount is summed across items into /form8283TotalDeductionForFilingTest, so a negative entry here would net DOWN another item's amount and could switch /form8283ReturnFilesThisForm off on a return the statute requires the form for. The reductions the instructions require are applied BEFORE the amount is entered, which is why the floor is zero rather than a negative-adjustment slot.

Fact.Name: Section B property letter for the partial-interest statement
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 4a, letter A, B, or C identifying the property for which less than an entire interest was given.

Fact.Name: Partial-interest deduction for this tax year
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 4b(1), total amount claimed as a deduction for the listed property for this tax year.

Fact.Name: Partial-interest deduction for prior tax years
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 4b(2), total amount claimed as a deduction for the listed property for any prior tax years.

Fact.Name: Prior-year donee name (Form 8283 Section B Part II)
Fact.Description: Screen: "What is the name of the organization that received your prior-year contribution?" -- Section B Part II line 4c prints this only when a prior year's contribution of an interest in the SAME property went to an organization different from the current donee named in Part I; the box is left blank whenever there was no prior-year gift or it went to the same donee. Help text: copy the name exactly as the prior year's Form 8283 or the organization's own acknowledgment states it. Asked beside the address question below, whenever the filer says a different organization received an earlier interest in this property. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED to a blank box, not refused: the printed cell is left empty and no computed figure on the return moves. Validation on this screen: optional single-line text, no format. Feeds the Part II "Name of charitable organization (donee)" printed cell through /form8283Items/*/sectionBPriorYearDoneeName, which blanks the cell on a Section A copy. REPLACES /form8283Items/*/writablePriorYearDoneeNameAndAddress, which asked for a name AND an address in one answer and could not fill the printed form's three separate boxes (name, street, city/state/ZIP).

Fact.Name: Prior-year donee address (Form 8283 Section B Part II)
Fact.Description: Screen: "What is that organization's address?" -- the mailing address of the prior-year donee named above, printed on Section B Part II line 4c across a street box and a city/state/ZIP box. Help text: copy the address exactly as the prior year's Form 8283 or the organization's own acknowledgment states it. Asked directly beside the prior-year donee name question, whenever that question is asked. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED to a blank box, not refused: the printed cells are left empty and no computed figure on the return moves. Validation on this screen: a standard address (street, city, state, ZIP); no format beyond the ordinary address rules. Feeds the Part II "Address" and "City or town, state, and ZIP code" printed cells through /form8283Items/*/sectionBPriorYearDoneeAddress, split the same way the appraiser's and the acknowledging donee's business addresses already split into two boxes, which blanks both cells on a Section A copy. Together with .../writablePriorYearDoneeName, REPLACES /form8283Items/*/writablePriorYearDoneeNameAndAddress.

Fact.Name: Location of tangible property
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 4d, place where tangible property is located or kept.

Fact.Name: Other person having actual possession of the property
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 4e, name of any person other than the donee having actual possession.

Fact.Name: Restriction on donee's use or disposition
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 5a, whether a temporary or permanent restriction limits the donee's right to use or dispose of the property.

Fact.Name: Third-party rights to income, possession, voting, acquisition, or designation
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 5b, whether another person received a listed right relating to the donated property.

Fact.Name: Restriction limiting property to a particular use
Fact.Description: Section B, Part II line 5c, whether a restriction limits the donated property to a particular use.

Fact.Name: Donor statement item at appraised value of $500 or less
Fact.Description: Section B, Part III: description of each item that the appraisal identifies as having a value of $500 or less, with the identifying letter from Part I.

Fact.Name: Donor statement's Section B item letter
Fact.Description: Identifying letter from Section B, Part I for the donor's $500-or-less item statement.

Fact.Name: Donor signature
Fact.Description: Donor's signature for the Section B, Part III taxpayer statement; signature is a filer-supplied text value and is not generated by the module.

Fact.Name: Donor signature date
Fact.Description: Date the taxpayer signs the Section B, Part III statement.

Fact.Name: Appraiser signature
Fact.Description: Appraiser signature for the Section B, Part IV declaration.

Fact.Name: Appraiser name (Form 8283 Section B Part IV)
Fact.Description: Screen: "What is the name of the appraiser who signed your appraisal?" — the appraiser's name exactly as it is written on the qualified appraisal, which is what the printed Part IV "Appraiser name" box carries. Help text: this is the person or firm that valued the property, never the donor and never the charity — the printed declaration above the box has the appraiser swear they are none of those. Copy the name from the signed appraisal rather than retyping it, because the IRS reads this box against the appraisal document itself. Asked whenever a contributed item is going to print in Section B, which is the over-$5,000 section. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED to a blank box, not refused: the printed cell is left empty and no computed figure on the return moves, so a filer who has not yet received the appraisal can still file every other line. Validation on this screen: optional single-line text, no format. Feeds the Part IV "Appraiser name" printed cell through /form8283Items/*/sectionBAppraiserName, which blanks the cell on a Section A copy.

Fact.Name: Appraiser title (Form 8283 Section B Part IV)
Fact.Description: Screen: "What is that appraiser's title?" — the professional title printed beside the appraiser's name in Part IV, for example Accredited Senior Appraiser, or Partner. Help text: the title is how the appraiser states the qualification the declaration above the box relies on ("because of my qualifications as described in the appraisal, I am qualified to make appraisals of the type of property being valued"), so copy it from the appraisal. Leave it empty if the appraisal shows none. Asked beside the appraiser-name question, whenever a contributed item is going to print in Section B. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED to a blank box, not refused: the cell prints empty and no computed figure moves. Validation on this screen: optional single-line text, no format. Feeds the Part IV "Title" printed cell through /form8283Items/*/sectionBAppraiserTitle, which blanks the cell on a Section A copy.

Fact.Name: Appraiser business address
Fact.Description: Appraiser's business address in Section B, Part IV.

Fact.Name: Appraiser identifying number
Fact.Description: Appraiser identifying number in Section B, Part IV.

Fact.Name: Appraiser signature date
Fact.Description: Date the appraiser signs the Section B, Part IV declaration.

Fact.Name: Date donee received donated property
Fact.Description: Section B, Part V date on which the charitable organization received the property described in Part I.

Fact.Name: Donee intends unrelated use
Fact.Description: Section B, Part V, whether the organization intends to use the property for an unrelated use.

Fact.Name: Donee acknowledging organization name
Fact.Description: Section B, Part V name of charitable organization and employer identification number.

Fact.Name: Donee employer identification number
Fact.Description: Employer identification number for the Section B, Part V donee organization.

Fact.Name: Donee address in the acknowledgment
Fact.Description: Section B, Part V address of the acknowledging charitable organization.

Fact.Name: Donee authorized signature
Fact.Description: Authorized representative's signature acknowledging receipt of the Section B property.

Fact.Name: Donee authorized representative's title (Form 8283 Section B Part V)
Fact.Description: Screen: "What is the title of the person who signed the charity's acknowledgment?" — the title printed beside the authorized signature in Part V, for example Executive Director, or Treasurer. Help text: the charity completes and signs Part V; you copy what it wrote. The title is the charity's evidence that the signer could bind it to the Form 8282 undertaking printed above the line. Asked whenever a contributed item is going to print in Section B and the filer has the signed acknowledgment in hand. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED to a blank box, not refused: the cell prints empty and no computed figure on the return moves. Validation on this screen: optional single-line text, no format. Feeds the Part V "Title" printed cell through /form8283Items/*/sectionBDoneeAuthorizedTitle, which blanks the cell on a Section A copy.

Fact.Name: Donee authorized signature date (Form 8283 Section B Part V)
Fact.Description: Screen: "On what date did the charity sign its acknowledgment?" — the date written beside the authorized signature at the foot of Part V. Help text: this is the date the charity signed the form, which is not the same as the date it received the property; that one is asked separately and prints inside the acknowledgment paragraph. Asked beside the donee-title question. Unanswered ⇒ DEFAULTED and nothing is lost on the filed page: the printed Part V "Date" caption HAS NO fillable AcroForm field on the TY2025 template, so this answer cannot be rendered by the register at all and is held for the externally-signed or Form 8453 route. No computed figure on the return reads it. Validation on this screen: optional single-line text; the application should collect it as a date and hand it over formatted. Feeds no printed cell on the TY2025 template.

Fact.Name: Total claimed noncash deduction before income-limit carryover
Fact.Description: Total amount claimed across the entered noncash property items, before applying income limits that may create a carryover. An entered contribution with no claimed-deduction amount keeps this sum Incomplete; an empty item collection sums to zero, and so does an ABSENT one: a bare CollectionSum over a collection that was never created resolves Placeholder, not Complete, so the absent case is answered first and explicitly. Each addend is floored at zero, so a negative entry on one item cannot cancel a positive one out of the filing test and hide a form the return owes. This total must never be added to Schedule A, which computes the charitable deduction itself.

Fact.Name: Return files Form 8283
Fact.Description: True when the complete total deduction for contributed property is over $500; a listed item with no claimed-deduction amount stays Incomplete rather than silently suppressing the form. A charitable carryover year ALSO requires the form on its own: the instructions say to file Form 8283 for any carryover year described in IRC 170(d), whatever was contributed this year, so an answered-true carryover makes this fact true before the amount is even looked at. An answered-false or unanswered carryover takes nothing away and the amount test decides alone. A pass-through allocation ALSO requires the form on its own: an item answered as a share allocated by an entity that filed its own Form 8283 means the entity contribution was over $500, and the instructions have every member complete and attach a separate form for it, so such an item makes this fact true whatever the member share is. A true filing obligation is not proof that every required item detail, signature or attached statement is ready.

Fact.Name: This property is a share allocated by a pass-through entity that filed its own Form 8283
Fact.Description: TRUE when this item's reporting treatment is answered as a pass-through allocation; FALSE when the treatment is answered as anything else or is unanswered, so an undecided item never forces the form on its own. Read by the pass-through arm of the return-level filing test.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 item is in the filed population
Fact.Description: Every property item is rendered only when the return-level $500 filing test is true.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 copies to render, one per contribution item
Fact.Description: Filtered view used by includeForEach. One copy per entered item is within the form's "one or more Forms 8283" instruction and avoids exceeding the four Section A / three Section B rows; a group of similar items can remain a single item.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 reporting-treatment categories
Fact.Description: The categories the printed section instructions turn on. Each names a rule in the instructions, not a conclusion about whether a charitable deduction is allowed: the five Section A exception categories (the three published-quotation security tests taken together, the regulatory other-security exception, an acknowledged gross-proceeds vehicle, intellectual property, and inventory), the poor-condition clothing or household article the instructions send to Section B over $500, a partial-interest or restricted-use contribution, a pass-through allocation that follows the entity's section, and ordinary property, which is everything else and is decided on the amount alone. THE CATEGORIES ARE EXCLUSIVE AND ORDERED BY THE INSTRUCTIONS: partial interest or restricted use is chosen ahead of an inventory or security label, because the instructions say to use Section B even when the property the partial interest was carved from was held primarily for sale to customers.

Fact.Name: Reporting treatment of this donated property (writable)
Fact.Description: Which of the printed instruction categories this property falls in. It is a FACTUAL intake about the property, not a legal inference from its description: a security counts as publicly traded only if it meets one of the three published-quotation tests the instructions print, the other-security category requires the regulatory exception the instructions cross-reference, the vehicle category requires BOTH that the deduction is limited to the gross proceeds of the sale AND that a contemporaneous written acknowledgment was obtained, and the intellectual-property and inventory categories are only the property the instructions define. A single article of clothing or a household item not in good used condition or better is the poor-condition category. Choose partial interest or restricted use ahead of any ordinary category. Choose pass-through when this share was allocated by an entity that filed its own Form 8283. Unanswered leaves the section undecided, which leaves both printed sections blank rather than guessing one.

Fact.Name: Claimed deduction for this item or its whole group of similar items (writable)
Fact.Description: The total claimed deduction, before the income limits that could create a carryover, for this item or for the entire group of similar items it belongs to, INCLUDING the parts given to other donee organizations. The instructions say to consider all items in the group even when they went to more than one donee, and then to file a separate Section B for each donee, which is why the group total decides the section while each donee keeps its own copy. For a standalone item this is that item's own claimed deduction. It is never summed across items and never reaches Schedule A, which computes the deduction itself. Nonnegative; an amount below this item's own claimed deduction contradicts itself and leaves the section undecided rather than picking one.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 is required for a charitable carryover year (writable)
Fact.Description: Does this return carry a charitable contribution forward from an earlier year under IRC 170(d)? The instructions require Form 8283 for any such carryover year, independently of what was contributed this year, so a true answer makes the form required even when this year's noncash total is at or below the filing threshold. An unanswered entry establishes no carryover obligation, and a false one takes nothing away: the this-year threshold test still decides on its own.

Fact.Name: Claimed deduction for this item, floored at zero
Fact.Description: The entered claimed deduction floored at zero, so that a negative entry on one item cannot cancel a positive one out of the filing total and cannot pull an item below a section threshold. The floor is in this body and not on the Writable because a Limit is validation on the entry screen and is not enforced when the graph resolves. An unanswered claimed deduction stays Incomplete here; this is not a Schedule A deduction computation.

Fact.Name: A claimed deduction for clothing or a household item not in good used condition, at $500 or less
Fact.Description: TRUE when this item is clothing or a household item not in good used condition or better and its claimed deduction is more than $0 but not more than $500. No deduction is allowed for such an item; the only exception is a single item claimed at more than $500 with a qualified appraisal, which goes to Section B. FALSE, never Incomplete, while the treatment or the claimed deduction is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Refusal: a deduction claimed for clothing or a household item not in good used condition, at $500 or less
Fact.Description: We can't file this return: it claims a charitable deduction for clothing or a household item that is not in good used condition or better, valued at $500 or less. The law allows no deduction for such an item. Remove it from your charitable contributions, or, if it is in good used condition or better, change its description. A single item claimed at more than $500 is deductible only with a qualified appraisal attached, and that is reported in Section B.

Fact.Name: The deduction the Form 8283 section threshold is applied to
Fact.Description: The item-or-group total this item's section is decided on: the entered group total, accepted only when both amounts are answered and the group total is at least this item's own floored deduction. A group total below the item it contains contradicts itself, and an unanswered group total says nothing, so both leave this Incomplete and the section undecided. It is used for the section decision only and is never summed across items.

Fact.Name: The Form 8283 section this property must be reported in
Fact.Description: Section A or Section B, decided from the reporting category and the item-or-group deduction in the order the printed instructions state them. A pass-through allocation takes the section the entity used, which the instructions say a member must match. A single article of clothing or a household item not in good used condition or better goes to Section B whenever the deduction is OVER $500, which is why exactly $500 falls through to the ordinary amount test. The five Section A exception categories stay in Section A whatever the amount. Everything else turns on the item-or-group total: at or below $5,000 Section A, above $5,000 Section B. The boundary is the printed one, not a rounded one: $5,000 is Section A and $5,001 is Section B. An undecided category or an undecided group total runs off the end of this Switch and leaves the section Incomplete, which prints the item in NEITHER section; there is deliberately no catch-all, because a default section would put a property in front of the IRS under a rule nobody applied. This decides printed placement only. It never changes the deduction.

Fact.Name: This property prints in Form 8283 Section A
Fact.Description: True exactly when the computed section for this property is Section A. An undecided section leaves this Incomplete, and every Section A column projection runs off its own Switch on that, so the printed cells stay blank rather than carrying a value into a section nobody chose.

Fact.Name: This property belongs in the Form 8283 Section A print collection
Fact.Description: True when this return files Form 8283 AND this property belongs in Section A. A return that does not file the form answers false without ever needing a section, so an item whose category was never entered does not hold up a return that attaches nothing. Once the form IS filed, an undecided section leaves this Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A contribution items
Fact.Description: The filed items that belong in Section A, in the order they were entered. It exists so a reviewer and a future register packing pass can see which items land in which section; the shipping register still renders one copy per item off /form8283ItemsToPrint and fills only the cells of the section that item belongs to.

Fact.Name: This property prints in Form 8283 Section B
Fact.Description: True exactly when the computed section for this property is Section B. An undecided section leaves this Incomplete, and every Section B column projection runs off its own Switch on that, so the printed cells stay blank rather than carrying a value into a section nobody chose.

Fact.Name: This property belongs in the Form 8283 Section B print collection
Fact.Description: True when this return files Form 8283 AND this property belongs in Section B. A return that does not file the form answers false without ever needing a section, so an item whose category was never entered does not hold up a return that attaches nothing. Once the form IS filed, an undecided section leaves this Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B contribution items
Fact.Description: The filed items that belong in Section B, in the order they were entered. It exists so a reviewer and a future register packing pass can see which items land in which section; the shipping register still renders one copy per item off /form8283ItemsToPrint and fills only the cells of the section that item belongs to.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (a), the donee organization name, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (a), the donee organization name cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. The register renders one copy per contribution item and a register mapping cannot switch on the section, so each printed cell reads its own section-gated projection: this fact is the item's own writableDoneeOrganizationName when the item prints in Section A, and Incomplete otherwise, which leaves the opposite section's cells empty on the same copy.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (a), the donee organization address, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (a), the donee organization address cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. The register renders one copy per contribution item and a register mapping cannot switch on the section, so each printed cell reads its own section-gated projection: this fact is the item's own writableDoneeOrganizationAddress when the item prints in Section A, and Incomplete otherwise, which leaves the opposite section's cells empty on the same copy. The printed cell carries a name and an address together; the register composes the two projections into the one box.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (b), the vehicle checkbox, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (b), the vehicle checkbox cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (c), the description of the donated property, for this property

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (c), the condition of the donated property, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (c), the condition of the donated property cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (h), the fair market value cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section A line 1 column (i), the method used to determine the fair market value, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section A line 1 column (i), the method used to determine the fair market value cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section A. Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B Part I line 3 column (a), the description of the donated property, for this property

The register renders one copy per contribution item and a register mapping cannot switch on the section, so each printed cell reads its own section-gated projection: this fact is the item's own writablePropertyDescription when the item prints in Section B, and Incomplete otherwise, which leaves the opposite section's cells empty on the same copy.

Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B Part II, the prior-year donee name box, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section B Part II line 4c "Name of charitable organization (donee)" cell for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section B. The register renders one copy per contribution item and a register mapping cannot switch on the section, so each printed cell reads its own section-gated projection: this fact is the item's own writablePriorYearDoneeName when the item prints in Section B, and Incomplete otherwise, which leaves this page-two cell empty on a Section A copy. Fact.Name: Form 8283 Section B Part II line 5a, the Yes box, for this property
Fact.Description: The Section B Part II line 5a "Yes" box for this property, blank unless the property belongs in Section B. The register renders one copy per contribution item and a register mapping cannot switch on the section, so each printed cell reads its own section-gated projection: this fact is the item's own writableRestrictionOnDoneeUseOrDisposition when the item prints in Section B, and Incomplete otherwise, which leaves this page-two cell empty on a Section A copy. There is no catch-all arm, so an undecided section also leaves the cell blank rather than printing a restriction answer under a rule nobody applied. The printed question is a Yes/No pair and the register binds one box to each side, so this projection carries the Yes box and /form8283Items/*/sectionBNoRestrictionOnDoneeUseOrDisposition carries the No box. An unanswered question leaves BOTH boxes unchecked, which is the printed posture of a donor who has not answered.
